clue.text: Standard overseas march

definitions.meaning: a standard is a flag; overseas points to the United States
Sousa's well-known military march is named after the American flag

explanation.surface: A banner abroad accompanies a military parade.
explanation.definitionFit: The US national flag carries this name, and Sousa's famous march is titled after that flag.

clue.text: CO?

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, but C stands first in the word command and O stands next to it

explanation.walkthrough: CO looks like the abbreviation for a commanding officer; read instead as letters, C is first in 'command' and O comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy officer ranks just below the commander, which mirrors O sitting just after C in the word.

clue.text: Moan in bed troubled by stomach?

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restless sleeper groans in bed with a sore tummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' shuffles MOAN and BED together; 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly or tummy, the region holding the stomach, is the anatomical term here; the question mark admits the looseness.

clue.text: RU Club for disposal at reduced prices

definitions.meaning: RU is rugby union; the Cheshire town of ... has a well-known rugby union side
a shop clearance where goods are cut in price

explanation.surface: A rugby club clears out its stock cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Sale Sharks is an English rugby union club near Manchester, and a discount event in shops bears the same name.

clue.text: What delicate shades of colour

parts.note: the whole clue describes fine gradations or subtle differences in tone

explanation.definitionFit: Subtle distinctions of tint or meaning are exactly what the word names.

clue.text: Author of No.10-mine's no disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes an appearance, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists their cover is genuine and not a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No.10' points to 10-across, the detective; the anagram of MINES NO under 'disguise' gives his creator.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was the Belgian novelist who created Inspector Maigret, the detective at 10-across.

clue.text: Maugham's story of painter finally accepted socially

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
to be in is to be fashionable or welcomed by society

explanation.surface: A Maugham tale about an artist who at last wins a place in high society.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is a stock crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset Maugham's short story set in Pago Pago, later filmed, carries this weather title.

clue.text: Strangely, Royal Marine paid about end of July to show the monument .

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the extra one
strangely signals the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A marine pays a visit to an ancient monument at the end of July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' scrambles RM and PAID; 'about' puts them round Y, taken by 'end of' from July.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian royal tomb with sloping triangular faces is a classic ancient monument.

clue.text: … possibly Tut's, on re-served ground — near Birm-birmingham

indicators.note: possibly signals an alternative arrangement of the letters

parts.note: food served a second time is usually leftovers eaten chilled
a ground for sport is a field

explanation.surface: Continuing from the monument clue, the boy king's tomb is pictured on a replayed pitch near Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 7-down's monument, suggesting Tutankhamun's. 'possibly' rearranges TUTSON; 'Birm-birmingham' is a print slip for Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in the West Midlands is a royal borough on the northern edge of Birmingham.

clue.text: When pitched below middle .C. it produces a hissing sound

definitions.text: When pitched below middle .C. it produces a hissing sound

parts.words: When pitched below middle .C. it produces a hissing sound
parts.note: musical pitch is a decoy: the mark is placed under the letter C, making it sound like S

explanation.walkthrough: 'middle C' and 'pitched' suggest music, but the mark sits under a written letter C, as in façade, giving it an S sound.
explanation.definitionFit: This hook-shaped diacritic under a C in French or Portuguese softens the letter to a sibilant.

clue.text: Sort of ragtime sleuth

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, putting the letters in order differently

explanation.surface: A detective who resembles a kind of syncopated jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Simenon's Paris police inspector is a famous fictional detective.

clue.text: Unfeeling, miners' body approaching Britons' leader

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Britons

explanation.surface: A heartless union of miners draws near the head of the British.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM, the National Union of Mineworkers, was Britain's coal miners' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Without sensation or feeling, as fingers in the cold, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Signs of bad cold? Here's topping stuff

definitions.meaning: a severe frost shows in ice building up on surfaces
the sweet layer spread on top of a cake

explanation.surface: Someone sniffling also notices a cake's decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice forming on wings or roads shows a hard frost, and the sugary coating on a cake is the same word.

clue.text: Shield boss from gumboils

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A protective boss suffers from mouth sores.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised central knob on a round shield is its boss, a term from Latin.

clue.text: Saline treatment practically destroys me

indicators.note: treatment suggests working the letters into another form
practically means almost, so the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A garden creature complains that salt nearly kills it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' trims SALINE to SALIN, which 'treatment' rearranges; the whole clue is the creature speaking, since salt kills it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners sprinkle salt on these slow shelled molluscs, which it dehydrates and kills.

clue.text: On the palate, say, it can be raw or burnt

definitions.text: On the palate, say, it can be raw or burnt

parts.words: On the palate, say, it can be raw or burnt
parts.note: palate is heard as the painter's palette, and raw and burnt are the two forms of this brown pigment

explanation.walkthrough: Raw and burnt suggest food on the tongue, but 'say' means palate stands for palette; raw and burnt are the two grades of this earth pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: This brown earth pigment is sold in two forms, the raw version and a roasted, darker one.

clue.text: Spell "increase say, for striker

definitions.meaning: a period or turn of activity
the striker is the batter facing the bowler, standing at the crease for a batting turn

explanation.surface: A batsman spends a period at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The striker in cricket is the batter receiving the ball; the crease is the line marked at the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A batting turn in cricket is a spell at the wicket, while the striker stands in the crease to face the bowling.

clue.text: Domain uncertain — starting circuit?

indicators.note: uncertain indicates the letters are unsettled and rearranged
starting means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A traveller with no fixed territory sets off on a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' rearranges DOMAIN, and 'starting' adds C from circuit; the whole clue describes a wandering people with no fixed home setting out on a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering peoples have no settled territory and travel a seasonal round, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Trust this harvester

definitions.meaning: a commercial grouping of firms acting together
the farm machine that reaps and threshes in one pass

explanation.surface: A farmer has confidence in the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A business cartel is a trust in the old commercial sense, and the grain-reaping machine is named the same.

clue.text: Crane observed from Arab outposts

indicators.note: observed means the letters can be seen within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wading bird is spotted from desert lookout posts.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African stork is loosely a crane-like wading bird.

clue.text: Shepherd's charge — all the poor man had

definitions.meaning: a young female sheep in a shepherd's keeping
in the prophet Nathan's parable to King David, the poor man owned a single little female sheep

explanation.surface: A shepherd's flock was all a poor man owned.
explanation.definitionFit: A young female sheep is in a shepherd's care, and in Nathan's parable in Samuel the poor man owned only one such animal.

clue.text: Altogether the most superior thing one can wear

definitions.meaning: in total, taking everything together

definitions.text: the most superior thing one can wear
definitions.meaning: a work coat worn on top of all other clothes sits over everything

explanation.surface: Taken as a whole, the finest garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means in total, and the protective coat goes over everything else, so it is literally above all.

clue.text: A curl so in disarray-it's from kissing (7) 221It was said on meeting en D timely rotten weather

indicators.note: in disarray means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ringlet is tousled after a passionate kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text runs on into the next clue; only 'A curl so in disarray — it's from kissing' belongs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculation is the formal word for kissing, so the adjective means relating to it.

clue.text: It was said on meeting entirely rotten weather

parts.note: pellets of ice falling from the sky make nasty weather

explanation.surface: A greeting at a meeting about wholly foul weather.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic salutation, as the witches greet Macbeth, was a greeting used when people met.

clue.text: Record token

definitions.meaning: to note down or register
a sign or symbol

explanation.surface: A note kept as a souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something down is to record it, and a sign or symbol of something is also the same word.

clue.text: Settle in court

definitions.meaning: a settle is a high-backed wooden seat
the judges or magistrates of a court collectively

explanation.surface: Resolve a dispute before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a long wooden seat, and in court the judges as a body are referred to by their seat.

clue.text: This staff character is cracked, almost

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short of its last letter

explanation.surface: An employee is said to be half-mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The staff is the musical stave, not a workforce; 'cracked' is split, losing its last letter by 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol at the start of a musical stave fixes the pitch of the lines.

clue.text: Examination of the mouth?

definitions.meaning: a spoken test, as in language exams
relating to the mouth, as in hygiene

explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test is so named, and the adjective also means relating to the mouth.

clue.text: King born in such a joint

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards
née is French for born, used before a maiden name

explanation.surface: A monarch was born in a pub of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge between thigh and shin is a leg joint.

clue.text: Consort with a following in Canada

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort

explanation.surface: Keep company with a group of followers in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consort' is the noun: Prince Albert, consort of Queen Victoria, after whose daughter the province is named.
explanation.definitionFit: This western prairie province of the country is named after Princess Louise Caroline Alberta.

clue.text: Our ancestry, i.e, Angle, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could form another word

explanation.surface: Someone muses that their family might descend from the Angles.
explanation.definitionFit: Line of descent from forebears is a person's ancestry.

clue.text: One way to describe a Lee- Enfield?

definitions.text: One way to describe a Lee- Enfield?

parts.words: One way to describe a Lee- Enfield?
parts.note: the Lee-Enfield is a single-barrel rifle, but its hyphenated name is like a hyphenated surname

explanation.walkthrough: The Lee-Enfield was the British Army's standard bolt-action rifle; it has one barrel, but its hyphenated name is like a posh hyphenated surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated surname is described this way, as is a shotgun with two barrels.
